question:
A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of amenorrhea for 4 months. Menses previously occurred at regular 28-day intervals and last for 3 to 4 days. There is no family history of serious illness. She receives good grades in school and is on the high school track team. She is sexually active with one male partner and uses condoms consistently. She appears thin. Examination shows bilateral parotid gland enlargement. There is fine hair over the trunk. Serum studies show:
Thyroid-stimulating hormone 3.7 μU/mL
Prolactin 16 ng/mL
Estradiol 23 pg/mL (N > 40)
Follicle-stimulating hormone 1.6 mIU/mL
Luteinizing hormone 2.8 mIU/mL
A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Amenorrhea for 4 months" -> "Regular menses previously" -> "Thyroid-stimulating hormone within normal range" -> "Possible thyroid dysfunction" -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: "Bilateral parotid gland enlargement" -> "Fine hair over the trunk" -> "Elevated prolactin levels" -> "Possible pituitary dysfunction" -> 60% confidence. CHAIN: "Low estradiol levels" -> "Low follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone levels" -> "Possible hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis dysfunction" -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: "Negative urine pregnancy test" -> "Excludes pregnancy-related causes" -> "Less likely to be exogenous steroid use" -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: "Thin appearance" -> "Possible nutritional deficiency" -> "Impaired hormone production" -> "Possible cause of the findings" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of the findings in the 17-year-old girl with amenorrhea, low estradiol, and hormonal imbalances is gonadal dysgenesis. This is supported by the low estradiol levels, low FSH and LH levels indicating hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis dysfunction, and the negative urine pregnancy test ruling out pregnancy-related causes. The presence of bilateral parotid gland enlargement, fine hair over the trunk, and elevated prolactin levels suggest possible pituitary dysfunction, further supporting the likelihood of gonadal dysgenesis.
